name: Great Disasters
description: Eruptions, earthquakes, fires, shipwrecks and accidents that the world remembers, from Pompeii to Fukushima.

checkpoints.name: Vesuvius to the Great Fire of London
checkpoints.note: Thera blows apart in the Bronze Age, Vesuvius buries Pompeii, the deadliest earthquake on record shakes China in 1556, and London burns in 1666.

checkpoints.name: Lisbon to Tunguska
checkpoints.note: Earthquakes, eruptions and floods are now written about across the world, and engineers learn from collapsing bridges and dams. Lisbon, Krakatoa and Galveston shape the first modern ideas of preparing for disaster, while the Yellow River flood of 1887 shows how rivers can kill on a vast scale.

checkpoints.name: Titanic and Hindenburg
checkpoints.note: Ships, airships and chemical works fail on a huge scale, and giant quakes in Chile and Alaska help prove plate tectonics. The great Chinese floods of 1931 and the Bhola cyclone of 1970 kill huge numbers. Governments begin to write new safety rules after each disaster.

checkpoints.name: Chernobyl to today
checkpoints.note: Nuclear plants, spacecraft and chemical factories bring risks no earlier century knew, while the world watches tsunamis and storms on live television and learns the cost of weak warnings. The Tangshan quake of 1976 and the Sichuan and Haiti quakes of 2008 and 2010 show how weak buildings raise the toll. In 2023 two great earthquakes in Turkey and Syria killed more than fifty thousand people.
